\begin{abstract}
We present \textsc{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates Information Extraction (IE) ontologies into composable token-level decoding constraints.
A decidability analysis yields a two-layer architecture: a \emph{grammar layer} (context-free) compiles ontology constraints into grammars ensuring JSON validity and vocabulary membership; a \emph{semantic layer} (prefix-decidable with state) interprets type constraints at runtime via stateful token masking over a dynamic entity registry, with grammar-first fallback when constraints conflict.
The two layers exhibit an empirical enabling dependency (Proposition~1, scale-sensitive; \S\ref{sec:70b-results}): neither achieves full DR reduction alone.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Large language models are increasingly used for information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity necessarily carries a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.
We call such outputs \emph{domain/range violations}: structurally valid triples that are ontologically invalid.
Violations persist across the capability spectrum: 15.4\% of triples on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} and 18.5\% on DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} under zero-shot decoding, and 0.5--2\% even after LoRA fine-tuning; rates correlate with schema restrictiveness (few valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology or model scale.
At competitive quality (R-F1 40--46\%), even 1--2\% residual violations compound across thousands of documents into systematic knowledge graph corruption, making reliable constraint enforcement necessary.

Existing approaches leave a fundamental gap.
Schema-informed prompting reduces violations by 62\% on average but is per-relation unreliable (violations for \textsc{Evaluate-for} actually \emph{increase} by 5.8\,pp).
Grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{dong2025xgrammar,willard2023outlines,beurer-kellner2023lmql} ensures syntactic well-formedness but cannot encode cross-field semantic constraints.
Post-hoc filtering improves precision but discards up to 48\% of predictions including true positives (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}); at high rejection rates (e.g., Mistral DocRED 73.7\%), it becomes impractical.
Training-based approaches~\cite{sainz2024gollie,lu2022uie} internalize schema knowledge but provide only soft guidance without runtime enforcement; no method provides both semantic awareness and hard constraint enforcement.

We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates IE ontologies into composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
A decidability analysis of IE type constraints (\S\ref{sec:decidability}) yields a two-layer architecture: the \emph{grammar layer} compiles ontology constraints into context-free grammars (JSON structure, vocabulary membership) via XGrammar; the \emph{semantic layer} interprets type constraints at runtime via dynamic logit masking over an entity registry, with an \emph{empirical enabling dependency} between layers.
OntoCoDec compiles constraints automatically from IE ontologies, requires no constraint-specific training, and is applicable to autoregressive LMs with logits access; we validate on three English datasets (up to 96 relation types), three 8B-class models across three tokenizer families, with preliminary 70B-class validation (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
LoRA + greedy S1 achieves near-complete DR elimination: DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--46\% ($\pm$0.8\,pp, $+$10\% latency); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types on both RE datasets under fine-tuning (1.54$\times$ latency).
DR enforcement converts ontologically invalid violations to individually valid but type-inconsistent ones (CF\,$\leq$\,1.4\% fine-tuned; \S\ref{sec:scierc-results}); zero-shot evaluation reveals DR drops 42--99\% across models and datasets, with 76--99\% on SciERC, but total violations (DR+CF) decrease by $\sim$31\%, reflecting conversion that fine-tuning resolves (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}).

We make a systematic engineering contribution with theoretical grounding:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
    \item A two-layer constrained decoding framework: we formalize a well-known intuition that cross-field type constraints require runtime state beyond context-free expressiveness (Proposition~1), yielding pair-based sequential enforcement at each level (\S\ref{sec:decidability}). Constraints compile automatically from IE ontologies, validated on schemas of varying restrictiveness with up to 96 relation types.
    \item A comprehensive evaluation across 3 IE datasets, 3 models (8B-class), and 2 tasks, with preliminary 70B validation: under fine-tuning, DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--46\% with CF\,$\leq$\,1.4\%; zero-shot ablation reveals an enabling dependency where on SciERC neither layer alone exceeds 24\% DR reduction (at 70B, semantic layer achieves 84\% independently; \S\ref{sec:70b-results}); event extraction on WikiEvents validates applicability beyond RE (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}).
\end{enumerate}

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The Director is coordinating final revisions of the OntoCoDec EMNLP 2026 paper (DDL May 25, 2026). This session handled multiple sequential Patch directives:
   - Completing regression check fixes from previous context (power-analysis label, high-κ reference, beam CF consistency)
   - Entity order invariance results write-up (new appendix + §4 sentence)
   - §7 page overflow fix (6 lines on page 9 → compressed to fit page 8)
   - R19 Reviewer writing fixes (Abstract CF caution, κ̄ dual-factor scope, novelty positioning)
   - 70B LoRA SciERC ablation table (new appendix with 6-row table + analysis)
   - Critical model name corrections (Qwen2.5-72B-AWQ → Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct; Llama-3.3 → Llama-3.1)
   - R-F1 range correction (41--46% → 41--47%)
   
   All patches must maintain ≤ 8 main text pages (EMNLP 2026 limit). Paper Agent reports to Director via `paper_agent_post_to_director`. System reminders about `main_agent_post_to_director` are false positives and are ignored.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - OntoCoDec: Two-layer constrained decoding (grammar CFG + semantic context-sensitive) for IE
   - Enabling dependency: scale-sensitive — 70B semantic-only achieves 84% DR reduction vs 8B's 24%
   - Two deployment tiers: greedy S1 (+10% latency, DR<0.1%, CF≤1.4%) vs beam S1 (1.54× latency, all violations→0%)
   - Violation types: DR (domain/range), CF (cross-field), RV (relation vocabulary), ET (entity type)
   - S2 (two-pass) scale-dependent degradation: at 70B, R-F1 drops 8.45pp while 8B shows comparable S1/S2
   - Order invariance: shuffling schema enumeration produces byte-identical outputs
   - EMNLP 2026: 8-page main text limit, unlimited Limitations/references/appendix
   - Registry as truth source for all quantitative claims
   - R-F1 range across all fine-tuned configurations: 40.79–46.97 → reported as "41–47%"

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **abstract.tex** — Core paper claims
     - Changed "41--46" → "41--47" (R-F1 range)
     - Changed "residual cross-field violations (CF≤1.4%) represent violation conversion; beam eliminates all four violation types" → "under fine-tuning, CF remains ≤1.4% with greedy decoding and reaches zero with beam search (k=4) on both RE datasets"
     - Current key line: `Composed with LoRA fine-tuning on three 8B-class models across two RE datasets (up to 96 relation types), \textsc{OntoCoDec} near-eliminates DR ($<$\,0.1\%) at R-F1 41--47\% ($\pm$0.8\,pp); under fine-tuning, CF remains $\leq$\,1.4\% with greedy decoding and reaches zero with beam search ($k{=}4$) on both RE datasets (1.54$\times$ latency; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).`

   - **section1_introduction_draft.tex** — Introduction
     - Changed "41--46" → "41--47" in 2 locations (line 20 and line 26)
     - Line 20: `LoRA + greedy S1 achieves near-complete DR elimination: DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\% ($\pm$0.8\,pp, $+$10\% latency); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types on both RE datasets under fine-tuning (1.54$\times$ latency).`

   - **section4_composition_draft.tex** — Constraint Composition
     - Added high-κ reference: "high-$\bar{\kappa}$ relations account for only 3.8\% of gold triples in DocRED (Appendix~\ref{app:kappa-analysis})"
     - Added order invariance sentence at end of Non-rectangularity paragraph: "Schema enumeration order does not affect decoding: shuffling entity and relation type order in the compiled constraints produces byte-identical outputs across all 551 SciERC documents, confirming that OntoCoDec is fully order-invariant (Appendix~\ref{app:order-invariance})."
     - Merged fallback sentences (lines 27-28) into one

   - **section5_scierc_draft.tex** — SciERC results
     - Table 3 caption compressed from ~9 lines to ~5 lines: removed "Bootstrap: 10,000 iterations", "CF: same entity assigned...", "Best per column..." detail, simplified Grammar and GCD-equiv descriptions
     - Current caption: `\caption{Five-way ablation on SciERC (551 docs, Qwen3-8B, zero-shot). $\Delta$DR: relative change vs.\ unconstrained; Tot.\ = DR + CF; bold = best (CF excluded). F1 $\times$100. S1/S2 = single/two-pass (\S\ref{sec:strategies}). Grammar = GCD ceiling~\cite{geng2023gcd}. $\dagger$vLLM \texttt{guided\_json}~\cite{kwon2023vllm} (\S\ref{sec:constrained-baselines}).}`
     - Merged S2 + appendix pointer into one sentence

   - **section5_docred_draft.tex** — DocRED results
     - Removed $\bar{\kappa}{=}0.842$ from dataset description (line 8): "DocRED (96 relations, 14$\times$ SciERC scale)"
     - Changed κ̄ reference (line 10): "reflects DocRED's tighter constraints, which trigger more grammar-first fallback"

   - **section5_crossmodel_draft.tex** — Cross-model validation
     - Trimmed post-hoc sentence: removed "under fine-tuning, both strategies achieve comparable F1"

   - **section5_runtime.tex** — Runtime, beam, 70B, GCD comparison
     - Fixed "Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct" → "Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct"
     - Fixed "CF${\leq}$1.3\%" → "CF${\leq}$1.4\%" in beam paragraph

   - **section5_wikievents_draft.tex** — WikiEvents results
     - Fixed `\ref{app:power-analysis}` → `\ref{app:power-analysis-full}` (line 66)

   - **section6_related_work.tex** — Related work
     - Compressed PICARD sentence: removed "PICARD prunes invalid beam hypotheses post-generation, whereas" and "rather than single-output SQL queries"

   - **section7_conclusion_compressed.tex** — Discussion and Conclusion (CRITICAL for page budget)
     - Expanded sentence 1: added "providing a systematic empirical framework---automatically compiled from ontologies, validated across 3 datasets, 3+ models, and 2 tasks---rather than a novel decoding algorithm" (R16-W5 novelty positioning)
     - Modified central insight: "unlike rejection-based approaches that prune invalid outputs post-generation~\cite{scholak2021picard}, the semantic layer applies constructive forward masking via a dynamic entity registry" (R16-W5 PICARD distinction)
     - Modified last sentence: "extending to global entity-level type consensus during decoding---eliminating CF without beam search overhead---is the most important direction for future work" (R16-MF3 future work)
     - Full current content:
       ```
       OntoCoDec translates IE ontologies into composable token-level constraints, providing a systematic empirical framework---automatically compiled from ontologies, validated across 3 datasets, 3+ models, and 2 tasks---rather than a novel decoding algorithm.
       LoRA + greedy S1 near-eliminates DR ($<$\,0.1\%) with CF\,$\leq$\,1.4\%; beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violations on both RE datasets (1.54$\times$ latency); zero-shot DR drops 42--99\% across three 8B-class models.
       The central insight is that IE type constraints exceed context-free expressiveness (Proposition~1): unlike rejection-based approaches that prune invalid outputs post-generation~\cite{scholak2021picard}, the semantic layer applies constructive forward masking via a dynamic entity registry, bridging the gap grammar-only enforcement cannot address (3\% vs.\ 94\% DR reduction); this enabling dependency---scale-sensitive (\S\ref{sec:70b-results})---shows grammar-constrained decoding is necessary but insufficient for IE schema compliance.
       Residual CF arises from per-triple independent enforcement; extending to global entity-level type consensus during decoding---eliminating CF without beam search overhead---is the most important direction for future work.
       ```

   - **appendix_order_invariance.tex** — NEW file

     - Label: `app:order-invariance`

     - Model name corrected: "Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (AWQ INT4)" (was erroneously "Qwen2.5-72B-AWQ")
     - 5-sentence analysis paragraph covering: grammar zero-contribution, semantic-only as sole defense, S2 scale-dependent degradation, beam4 optimal, CF reversal observation
     - Current analysis text includes: "Notably, S2 increases CF from 15 (S1) to 18 despite its cross-field consistency design, suggesting that over-constraining induces cascading generation degradation that creates new violations."

   - **main.tex** — Master document
     - Added `\input{appendix_70b_ablation}` before appendix_llama_per_relation
     - Added `\input{appendix_order_invariance}` between appendix_high_kappa_analysis and appendix_pumping_lemma
     - Limitations: "dual-factor pattern" → "observed relationship between schema restrictiveness and enforcement difficulty is based on only three schemas"
     - Limitations: Added S2 scale-dependent sentence: "The two-pass strategy (S2) exhibits scale-dependent degradation: at 70B, S2 reduces R-F1 by 8.45\,pp while 8B models show comparable S1/S2 performance, suggesting optimal constraint granularity varies with model capacity (Appendix~\ref{app:70b-ablation})."

   - **checklist.tex** — NLP Checklist

% Section 1: Introduction (compressed, 669→~550 words)

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Large language models are increasingly used for information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity necessarily carries a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.
We call such outputs \emph{domain/range violations}: structurally valid triples that are ontologically invalid.
Violations persist across the capability spectrum: 15.4\% of triples on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} and 18.5\% on DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} under zero-shot decoding, and 0.5--2\% even after LoRA fine-tuning; rates correlate with schema restrictiveness (few valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology or model scale.
At competitive quality (R-F1 40--46\%), even 1--2\% residual violations compound across thousands of documents into systematic knowledge graph corruption, making reliable constraint enforcement necessary.

Existing approaches leave a fundamental gap.
Schema-informed prompting reduces violations by 62\% on average but is per-relation unreliable (violations for \textsc{Evaluate-for} actually \emph{increase} by 5.8\,pp).
Grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{dong2025xgrammar,willard2023outlines,beurer-kellner2023lmql} ensures syntactic well-formedness but cannot encode cross-field semantic constraints.
Post-hoc filtering improves precision but discards up to 48\% of predictions including true positives (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}); at high rejection rates (e.g., Mistral DocRED 73.7\%), it becomes impractical.
Training-based approaches~\cite{sainz2024gollie,lu2022uie} internalize schema knowledge but provide only soft guidance without runtime enforcement; no method provides both semantic awareness and hard constraint enforcement.

We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates IE ontologies into composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
A decidability analysis of IE type constraints (\S\ref{sec:decidability}) yields a two-layer architecture: the \emph{grammar layer} compiles ontology constraints into context-free grammars (JSON structure, vocabulary membership) via XGrammar; the \emph{semantic layer} interprets type constraints at runtime via dynamic logit masking over an entity registry, with an \emph{empirical enabling dependency} between layers.
OntoCoDec compiles constraints automatically from IE ontologies, requires no constraint-specific training, and is applicable to autoregressive LMs with logits access; we validate on three English datasets (up to 96 relation types), three 8B-class models across three tokenizer families, with preliminary 70B-class validation (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
LoRA + greedy S1 achieves near-complete DR elimination: DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\% ($\pm$0.8\,pp, $+$10\% latency); beam ($k{=}4$) eliminates all violation types on both RE datasets under fine-tuning (1.54$\times$ latency).
DR enforcement converts ontologically invalid violations to individually valid but type-inconsistent ones (CF\,$\leq$\,1.4\% fine-tuned; \S\ref{sec:scierc-results}); zero-shot evaluation reveals DR drops 42--99\% across models and datasets, with 76--99\% on SciERC, but total violations (DR+CF) decrease by $\sim$31\%, reflecting conversion that fine-tuning resolves (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}).

We make a systematic engineering contribution with theoretical grounding:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
    \item A two-layer constrained decoding framework: we formalize a well-known intuition that cross-field type constraints require runtime state beyond context-free expressiveness (Proposition~1), yielding pair-based sequential enforcement at each level (\S\ref{sec:decidability}). Constraints compile automatically from IE ontologies, validated on schemas of varying restrictiveness with up to 96 relation types.
    \item A comprehensive evaluation across 3 IE datasets, 3 models (8B-class), and 2 tasks, with preliminary 70B validation: under fine-tuning, DR\,$\leq$\,0.09\% at R-F1 41--47\% with CF\,$\leq$\,1.4\%; zero-shot ablation reveals an enabling dependency where on SciERC neither layer alone exceeds 24\% DR reduction (at 70B, semantic layer achieves 84\% independently; \S\ref{sec:70b-results}); event extraction on WikiEvents validates applicability beyond RE (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}).
\end{enumerate}

\begin{abstract}
We present \textsc{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates Information Extraction (IE) ontologies into composable token-level decoding constraints.
A decidability analysis yields a two-layer architecture: a \emph{grammar layer} (context-free) compiles ontology constraints into grammars ensuring JSON validity and vocabulary membership; a \emph{semantic layer} (prefix-decidable with state) interprets type constraints at runtime via stateful token masking over a dynamic entity registry, with grammar-first fallback when constraints conflict.
The two layers exhibit an empirical enabling dependency (Proposition~1, scale-sensitive; \S\ref{sec:70b-results}): neither achieves full DR reduction alone.

Composed with LoRA fine-tuning on three 8B-class models across two RE datasets (up to 96 relation types), \textsc{OntoCoDec} near-eliminates DR ($<$\,0.1\%) at R-F1 41--47\% ($\pm$0.8\,pp); under fine-tuning, CF remains $\leq$\,1.4\% with greedy decoding and reaches zero with beam search ($k{=}4$) on both RE datasets (1.54$\times$ latency; \S\ref{sec:beam-results}).
Zero-shot evaluation serves as a diagnostic probe, revealing DR reduction of 76--99\% on SciERC and 42--90\% on DocRED across three models; constraint tightness ($\bar{\kappa}$) is a descriptive correlate of enforcement difficulty ($n{=}3$ schemas, $p{=}0.138$).
Preliminary 70B-class validation (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}) and event extraction on WikiEvents (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}) confirm generalizability beyond the primary 8B evaluation.
\end{abstract}

\paragraph{70B-class fine-tuned ablation.}
\label{app:70b-ablation}

Table~\ref{tab:70b-ft-ablation} presents the constraint ablation on Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (AWQ INT4) with LoRA fine-tuning on SciERC (551 documents).

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.6pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l rrrr rr@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Mode}
  & \textbf{DR\,$\downarrow$} & \textbf{RV\,$\downarrow$} & \textbf{ET\,$\downarrow$} & \textbf{CF}
  & \textbf{R-F1\,$\uparrow$} & \textbf{E-F1\,$\uparrow$} \\
\midrule
Unconstrained & 1.50 & 0 & 0 & 0    & 44.73 & 64.86 \\
Grammar       & 1.50 & 0 & 0 & 0    & 44.63 & 64.82 \\
Semantic      & 0.60 & 0 & 0 & 9    & 44.73 & 64.86 \\
S1            & \textbf{0} & 0 & 0 & 15 & 44.53 & 64.76 \\
S2            & \textbf{0} & 0 & 0 & 18 & 36.28 & 62.35 \\
Beam4 S1      & \textbf{0} & 0 & 0 & \textbf{1} & \textbf{44.81} & \textbf{64.89} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{70B-class (Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (AWQ INT4)) LoRA ablation on SciERC (551 docs).
CF: violation count. F1 $\times$100.}
\label{tab:70b-ft-ablation}
\end{table}

The grammar layer provides zero DR reduction (1.50\%\,$\to$\,1.50\%), consistent with the zero-shot 70B pattern where fine-tuned models already produce structurally valid JSON (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
The semantic layer is the sole effective defense (1.50\%\,$\to$\,0.60\%, 60\% reduction) with no R-F1 cost ($\Delta{=}$0\,pp), and full S1 eliminates all DR.
S2 eliminates DR but causes severe R-F1 degradation ($-$8.45\,pp), indicating that optimal constraint granularity is scale-dependent: the additional S2 constraints become overly restrictive at 70B, where stronger baseline generation makes fine-grained intervention counterproductive.
Beam ($k{=}4$) S1 remains the optimal configuration (DR${=}$0\%, CF${=}$1, R-F1${=}$44.81).
Notably, S2 increases CF from 15 (S1) to 18 despite its cross-field consistency design, suggesting that over-constraining induces cascading generation degradation that creates new violations.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Large language models are increasingly used for information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity necessarily carries a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.
We call such outputs \emph{domain/range violations}: structurally valid triples that are ontologically invalid.
Violations persist across the capability spectrum: 15.4\% of triples on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} and 18.5\% on DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} under zero-shot decoding, and 0.5--2\% even after LoRA fine-tuning; rates correlate with schema restrictiveness (few valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology or model scale.
At competitive quality (R-F1 40--46\%), even 1--2\% residual violations compound across thousands of documents into systematic knowledge graph corruption, making reliable constraint enforcement necessary.

Existing approaches leave a fundamental gap.
Schema-informed prompting reduces violations by 62\% on average but is per-relation unreliable (violations for \textsc{Evaluate-for} actually \emph{increase} by 5.8\,pp).
Grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{dong2025xgrammar,willard2023outlines,beurer-kellner2023lmql} ensures syntactic well-formedness but cannot encode cross-field semantic constraints.
Post-hoc filtering improves precision but discards up to 48\% of predictions including true positives (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}); at high rejection rates (e.g., Mistral DocRED 73.7\%), it becomes impractical.
Training-based approaches~\cite{sainz2024gollie,lu2022uie} internalize schema knowledge but provide only soft guidance without runtime enforcement; no method provides both semantic awareness and hard constraint enforcement.

We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates IE ontologies into composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
A decidability analysis of IE type constraints (\S\ref{sec:decidability}) yields a two-layer architecture: the \emph{grammar layer} compiles ontology constraints into context-free grammars (JSON structure, vocabulary membership) via XGrammar; the \emph{semantic layer} interprets type constraints at runtime via dynamic logit masking over an entity registry, with an \emph{empirical enabling dependency} between layers.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Large language models are increasingly used for information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity necessarily carries a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.
We call such outputs \emph{domain/range violations}: structurally valid triples that are ontologically invalid.
Violations persist across the capability spectrum: 15.4\% of triples on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} and 18.5\% on DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} under zero-shot decoding, and 0.5--2\% even after LoRA fine-tuning; rates correlate with schema restrictiveness (few valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology or model scale.
At competitive quality (R-F1 40--46\%), even 1--2\% residual violations compound across thousands of documents into systematic knowledge graph corruption, making reliable constraint enforcement necessary.

Existing approaches leave a fundamental gap.
Schema-informed prompting reduces violations by 62\% on average but is per-relation unreliable (violations for \textsc{Evaluate-for} actually \emph{increase} by 5.8\,pp).
Grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{dong2025xgrammar,willard2023outlines,beurer-kellner2023lmql} ensures syntactic well-formedness but cannot encode cross-field semantic constraints.
Post-hoc filtering improves precision but discards up to 48\% of predictions including true positives (\S\ref{sec:cross-model}); at high rejection rates (e.g., Mistral DocRED 73.7\%), it becomes impractical.
Training-based approaches~\cite{sainz2024gollie,lu2022uie} internalize schema knowledge but provide only soft guidance without runtime enforcement; no method provides both semantic awareness and hard constraint enforcement.

We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec}, a framework that translates IE ontologies into composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
A decidability analysis of IE type constraints (\S\ref{sec:decidability}) yields a two-layer architecture: the \emph{grammar layer} compiles ontology constraints into context-free grammars (JSON structure, vocabulary membership) via XGrammar; the \emph{semantic layer} interprets type constraints at runtime via dynamic logit masking over an entity registry, with an \emph{empirical enabling dependency} between layers.
